Lauren / team,

Quick triage from SRE: telemetry shows a sharp increase in egress retries and a correlated jump in KV cache miss amplification starting at 07:42 PDT for Pinnacle's primary region (us-east1/az1). Network graphs from edge-providers indicate packet loss at the AZ egress layer; upstream partner reported transient routing flaps at ~07:40. Service CPU and GPU utilization are normal.

Recommendation:
1) Initialize controlled drain of AZ1 for Pinnacle routes and shift traffic to us-west2 (pre-warmed pool). This will cause short-lived token rehydration (client will see increased latencies for first 30-60s while KV caches rebuild) but should eliminate 5xx flood.
2) Enable prefix/KV fallback: route new sessions to fallback model shard in us-west2, keep gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health checks between increments.
3) Monitor 95th latency and 5xxs in 5-minute windows; target 30-minute stabilization.

Risk/impact: expected transient 95th latency spike during cache warmup (30-90s windows); no expected data loss. If customer requires sticky session preservation we can use session affinity but that increases error surface.

ETA: engineer team can complete the controlled ramp in ~25 minutes once exec authorizes. Rollback plan: reverse ramp with same checks; if failover health checks do not pass at any step, we will pause and troubleshoot.

I'll be on the bridge.

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
